Amazon RDS for Oracle now supports Primary Endpoint
changes.detail: Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) for Oracle now provides a Primary Endpoint, a DNS name that always resolves to the current primary DB instance in a replica configuration. When you switch over to an Oracle replica, Amazon RDS points the Primary Endpoint to the new primary DB instance, so you don't need to change your application connection strings. Previously, after each switchover, you had to update connection strings or DNS records to point to the new primary DB instance, which often required change approvals and coordination across teams. changes.title: Amazon Cognito extends multi-Region replication to additional AWS Regions
changes.detail: Amazon Cognito multi-Region replication (MRR) now supports additional AWS Regions, extending the resilience benefits of MRR to more workloads. Amazon Cognito helps you implement secure sign-in and access control for users, AI agents, and microservices in minutes, and MRR lets you synchronize user and machine identity data, including credentials, user pool configurations, and federation setups, to a secondary user pool in a standby Region you designate in near real-time. changes.title: AWS Backup now supports incremental backups for Amazon DynamoDB
changes.detail: AWS Backup now supports incremental backups of Amazon DynamoDB tables, enabling you to reduce backup storage while maintaining backup schedules as frequent as one hour. Until now, AWS Backup created a full copy of your DynamoDB tables. With this launch, after an initial full backup, each incremental backup now captures only the data that changed, and AWS Backup takes a new full backup every 15 days. changes.detail: Improved blueprints: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio now gives project teams more ownership of their data and resources, within governance policies that administrators set centrally.
